name: nearest_neighbor_graph (k-nearest-neighbor graph of a spatial point set)

benchmarks.note: deterministic LCG scatter in the unit square, fixed k=3, Euclidean, directed, no cutoff. The kernel is an O(n^2 * d) all-pairs scan plus a per-source partial sort of in-cutoff candidates, so cost is quadratic in the point count: 50->200 (4x points) is ~17x time, 200->400 (2x points) is ~4.5x time, both tracking the n^2 expectation (the >4x and >16x factors come from the candidate-sort term growing with neighbor count per source)

fixed 300-point LCG scatter, Euclidean, directed, no cutoff, varying k. The dominant cost is the O(n^2) all-pairs distance scan, which is independent of k; k only affects the partial-selection and edge-emission term, so k=1->20 grows just ~17% (1.56ms->1.83ms) rather than linearly in k
